- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overshoot.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike in forecast after a recent dip, it often overcorrects; cap the spike at 1.2x recent high or 1.5x prior 30d mean.
- Model consistently under-forecasts in the first 5–7 days of a new trend (especially after negative sentiment), apply a 0.8–1.2x multiplier to early forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by strong positive moves, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7x the sentiment magnitude to forecast for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.15+), model often misjudges mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as anchor for correction.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >1.5% in 3+ consecutive days, apply a “reversion bias” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
